label: Luke 24:1
text: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they and some others came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.

label: Luke 24:2
text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.

label: Luke 24:3
text: They entered in, and didn’t find the Lord Jesus’ body.

variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': 'of the Lord Jesus' is read by P75, א, A, B, C and most witnesses; 'Jesus' by 579, 1071, 1241, syr cur; and τοῦ Ἰησοῦ is omitted entirely by D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, ff2, l, r1.

label: Luke 24:4
text: While they were greatly perplexed about this, behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.

label: Luke 24:5
text:
Becoming terrified, they bowed their faces down to the earth.
They said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?

label: Luke 24:6
text: He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,

variants.reading: 'He is not here, but is risen' (οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλ᾽ ἠγέρθη) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, ff2, l (Codex Rehdigerianus), r1, arm mss, geo B.

label: Luke 24:7
text: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”

label: Luke 24:8
text: They remembered his words,

label: Luke 24:9
text: returned from the tomb, and told all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.

variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by D, it a, b, c, d, e, ff2, l, r1, arm, geo.

label: Luke 24:10
text: Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James. The other women with them told these things to the apostles.

label: Luke 24:11
text: These words seemed to them to be nonsense, and they didn’t believe them.

label: Luke 24:12
text: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping and looking in, he saw the strips of linen lying by themselves, and he departed to his home, wondering what had happened.

variants.reading: the whole verse (Peter at the tomb) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': verse omitted by D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, l (Codex Rehdigerianus), r1 — one of the classic 'Western non-interpolations'.

label: Luke 24:13
text: Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.

variants.reading: ἑκατόν ἑξήκοντα, 'a hundred and sixty stadia' (about 30 km)
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': the hundred-sixty reading is attested by א (Sinaiticus), K*, N vid, Θ, Π, 079, 1079* pc and some lectionaries; the sixty reading of the standard text is carried by P75, A, B, D, E, F, G, H, K2, L, W, X, Δ, Ψ, 063, 070, f1, f13, Byz, Lect and most versions.

label: Luke 24:14
text: They talked with each other about all of these things which had happened.

label: Luke 24:15
text: While they talked and questioned together, Jesus himself came near, and went with them.

label: Luke 24:16
text: But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.

label: Luke 24:17
text:
He said to them,
“What are you talking about as you walk, and are sad?”

label: Luke 24:18
text: One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who doesn’t know the things which have happened there in these days?”

label: Luke 24:19
Luke 24:20
text: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.

label: Luke 24:21
text: But we were hoping that it was he who would redeem Israel. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.

label: Luke 24:22
text: Also, certain women of our company amazed us, having arrived early at the tomb;

label: Luke 24:23
text: and when they didn’t find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.

label: Luke 24:24
text: Some of us went to the tomb, and found it just like the women had said, but they didn’t see him.”

label: Luke 24:25
text:
He said to them,
“Foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!

label: Luke 24:26
text: Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”

label: Luke 24:27
text: Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

label: Luke 24:28
text: They came near to the village, where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.

label: Luke 24:29
text:
They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.”
He went in to stay with them.

label: Luke 24:30
text: When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.

label: Luke 24:31
text: Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he vanished out of their sight.

label: Luke 24:32
text: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”

label: Luke 24:33
text: They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,

label: Luke 24:34
text: saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”

label: Luke 24:35
text: They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.

label: Luke 24:36
text:
As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them,
“Peace be to you.”

variants.reading: 'and said to them: Peace unto you' (καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς εἰρήνη ὑμῖν) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': the phrase is read by mss of the Alexandrian, Caesarean and Byzantine text-types and bracketed by WH 1881 and Nestle 1904; omitted by D, it a, b, d, e, ff2, l, r1 and by Tischendorf's 8th edition. The same page records ὁ Ἰησοῦς ('Jesus') as omitted in the Alexandrian editions but present in Byz.

label: Luke 24:37
text: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

label: Luke 24:38
text:
He said to them,
“Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts?

label: Luke 24:39
text: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”

label: Luke 24:40
text: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

variants.reading: 'and having said thus, he showed to them the hands and the feet' (24:40) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': the verse is bracketed in the Alexandrian editions (WH 1881, Nestle 1904) and omitted by D, it a, b, d, e, ff2, l, r1, syr s, syr cur.

label: Luke 24:41
text:
While they still didn’t believe for joy, and wondered, he said to them,
“Do you have anything here to eat?”

label: Luke 24:42
text: They gave him a piece of a broiled fish and some honeycomb.

label: Luke 24:43
text: He took them, and ate in front of them.

label: Luke 24:44
text:
He said to them,
“This is what I told you, while I was still with you, that all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me must be fulfilled.”

label: Luke 24:45
text: Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.

label: Luke 24:46
text:
He said to them,
“Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead the third day,

label: Luke 24:47
text: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

label: Luke 24:48
text: You are witnesses of these things.

label: Luke 24:49
text: Behold, I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”

variants.reading: καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει, 'stay in the city' (Alexandrian) against 'stay in the city of Jerusalem' (Byz)
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': Alexandrian text-type (WH 1881, Tischendorf 8th, Nestle 1904) against Byz.

label: Luke 24:50
text: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.

variants.reading: ἕως πρὸς Βηθανίαν, 'as far as the vicinity of Bethany' (Alexandrian) for ἔξω ἕως εἰς Βηθανίαν, 'out as far as to Bethany' (Byz)
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': Alexandrian text-type against Byz (Stephanus TR 1550, Scrivener 1894, RP 2005).

label: Luke 24:51
text: While he blessed them, he withdrew from them, and was carried up into heaven.

variants.reading: 'and was carried up into heaven' (καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν) omitted
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by א* (Sinaiticus original hand), D (Codex Bezae), it a, b, d, e, ff2, l; hiatus in r1, syr s, syr cur, geo 1.

label: Luke 24:52
text: They worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,

variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': omitted by D, it a, b, d, e, ff2, l (hiatus in r1), syr s, syr cur, geo 2.

label: Luke 24:53
text: and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

variants.reading: αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεόν, 'praising God' (Western text-type) for 'blessing God'
variants.note: Per the fetched 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke': εὐλογοῦντες τὸν θεόν ('blessing God') is the Alexandrian reading of WH 1881, NA27/UBS4 and Nestle 1904; αἰνοῦντες ('praising') is the Western text-type. The WEB prints both: 'praising and blessing God'.

label: The women brought burial spices they had prepared to the tomb at early dawn on the first day of the week
statement: On the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared (24:1).

label: Two men in dazzling clothing appeared to the women at the tomb
statement: While the women were perplexed at the empty tomb, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing and asked why they seek the living among the dead (24:4-5).

label: The women reported the empty tomb to the eleven and were not believed
statement: The women returned from the tomb and told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest, but the words seemed to them nonsense and they did not believe them (24:9-11).

label: The women at the tomb were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James
statement: The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, with the other women with them, who told these things to the apostles (24:10).

label: Peter ran to the tomb and saw the linen strips lying by themselves
statement: Peter got up, ran to the tomb, stooped and looked in, saw the strips of linen (othonia) lying by themselves, and went home wondering (24:12); the verse is omitted by Codex Bezae and the Old Latin tradition.

label: Emmaus was a village sixty stadia from Jerusalem
statement: Two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia (about 11 km) from Jerusalem (24:13); some manuscripts (א original hand, K*, Θ, Π, 079) read 'a hundred sixty stadia' instead, and the village's identification is disputed.

label: One of the two on the Emmaus road was named Cleopas
statement: One of the two disciples walking to Emmaus answered Jesus and was named Cleopas (24:18); his companion is unnamed.

label: The risen Jesus walked unrecognized with the two to Emmaus and was recognized in the breaking of bread
statement: While the two talked, Jesus himself came near and went with them unrecognized; at table in Emmaus he took the bread, blessed, broke it and gave it to them, their eyes were opened, they recognized him, and he vanished out of their sight (24:15-31).

label: The two returned to Jerusalem and were told the Lord had appeared to Simon
statement: The two rose that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, found the eleven gathered with those with them, and were told 'The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon' (24:33-34).

label: The risen Jesus appeared to the gathered disciples in Jerusalem, showed his hands and feet and ate broiled fish
statement: While they spoke, Jesus himself stood among them in Jerusalem; he invited them to touch him, 'for a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones', showed his hands and feet, and ate a piece of broiled fish (and honeycomb in Byzantine witnesses) before them (24:36-43).

label: Jesus told the disciples to wait in Jerusalem until clothed with power from on high
statement: Jesus told the disciples: 'I send out the promise of my Father on you. But wait in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high' (24:49).

label: Jesus led the disciples out as far as Bethany and was carried up into heaven
statement: Jesus led them out as far as Bethany, lifted up his hands and blessed them, and while blessing them withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven (24:50-51); 'and was carried up into heaven' is omitted by the Sinaiticus original hand and the Western witnesses.

label: The disciples returned to Jerusalem and were continually in the temple blessing God
statement: They worshiped him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy, and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God (24:52-53).

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (candidate sites)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: Many sites have been suggested for the biblical Emmaus, among them Emmaus Nicopolis (c. 160 stadia from Jerusalem), Kiryat Anavim (66 stadia from Jerusalem on the carriage road to Jaffa ), Coloniya (c. 36 stadia on the carriage road to Jaffa), el-Kubeibeh (63 stadia, on the Roman road to Lydda )

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (manuscripts list different distances)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: The identification is complicated by the fact that New Testament manuscripts list at least three different distances between Jerusalem and Emmaus in Luke 24:13-14.

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (Eusebius and Jerome on Nicopolis)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: Eusebius was probably the first to mention Nicopolis as biblical Emmaus in his Onomasticon. Jerome , who translated Eusebius' book, implied in his letter 108 that there was a church in Nicopolis built in the house of Cleopas where Jesus broke bread on that late journey.

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (Imwas 153-161 stadia from Jerusalem)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: the village of Imwas was located at the end of the Ayalon Valley , on the border of the hill country of Judah , at 153 stadia (18.6 miles) from Jerusalem via the Kiryat Yearim Ridge Route, 161 stadia (19.6 miles) via the Beth-Horon Ridge Route

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (Josephus's War Emmaus, 30 stadia, 800 legionnaires)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: while in The Jewish War he brings up another Emmaus, just 30 Roman stadia from Jerusalem, where Vespasian settled 800 Roman legionnaires after the First Jewish Revolt .

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (Qubeibeh, 65 stadia close to Luke's 60)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: However, the Gospel of Luke speaks of 60 stadia [ 64 ] ( Luke 24:13 ), a distance very close to the actual 65 stadia to Qubeibeh.

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (no ancient source names Qubeibeh Emmaus)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: However, there is no source from the Roman, Byzantine or Early Muslim periods naming it as "Emmaus" for the time of Jesus.

label: Wikipedia: Emmaus (Abu Ghosh, celebration from the Crusader period)
title: Emmaus
excerpt: the memory of the apparition of the risen Jesus at Emmaus also started to be celebrated in three other places in the Holy Land: Motza (c. 4 mi or 6 km west of Jerusalem), Qubeibe (c. 7 mi or 11 km northwest of Jerusalem), and Abu Ghosh (c. 7 mi or 11 km west of Jerusalem).

label: Wikisource: Josephus, War 7.217 (Emmaus, 800 veterans, threescore furlongs)
title: The War of the Jews, Book VII (Whiston translation)
excerpt: However, he assigned a place for eight hundred men only, whom he had dismissed from his army, which he gave them for their habitation; it is called Emmaus, [ 13 ] and is distant from Jerusalem threescore furlongs.

label: Wikisource: Whiston's note on War 7.217 (Greek copies sixty, Latin thirty furlongs)
title: The War of the Jews, Book VII (Whiston translation), footnote citing Reland
excerpt: the Greek copies here usually make it sixty furlongs distant from Jerusalem, as does St. Luke, though the Latin copies say only thirty.
